A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same xLSTM scaling-law study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 672 training runs, fitted scaling laws, batch-size and fitting analyses, and measured inference timings.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds numerical training-configuration estimates derived from the existing fitted scaling laws.

M1.justification: The xLSTM and Transformer architectures, parametric loss model, IsoFLOP fitting procedure, and inference runtime model are retained. Newly specified packing and chunk settings document existing procedures rather than establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM-BASELINE language modeling and the same context-length and inference scenarios. Appendix E's estimates for larger models do not represent newly trained models, datasets, or evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Dense Llama-style Transformers remain the empirical comparator. The fixed-gamma versus fitted-gamma comparison in Figure 8 and analytical attention-cache comparisons in Table 7 are also retained.

E3.justification: The training-run corpus, model configurations, budgets, metrics, and inference measurement procedure are unchanged. First-fit packing and chunk size are newly disclosed settings, not reported revisions. Appendix E applies existing fits without reporting new training experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a limited derived analysis of how compute-optimal token-to-parameter ratios vary with model size and architecture, using Tables 23-25. Existing batch-size sensitivity and loss-fit analyses in Figures 7-8 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions average inference timings over four repetitions after two warm-up iterations. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-training counts, or uncertainty estimation for this work; the additional intervals quoted in Appendix E concern prior work.

E6.justification: Tables 23-25 add estimated optimal FLOPs, tokens, and ratios for models from 100M to 175B parameters. For example, Table 23 estimates 22.8B training tokens for a 1B Transformer versus 16.4B for xLSTM at context length 8192. These are derived predictions; existing measured results are retained. Section 3.5 also drops the cross-context performance-drop statement.

T1.justification: The scaling equations, FLOP and memory-operation derivations, and runtime assumptions are retained as v1 Appendices C-D become v2 Appendices B-C. Appendix E applies existing power laws without introducing new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The revised abstract emphasizes Pareto dominance, already claimed in v1's introduction, Section 3.2, and conclusion. The central claims about training efficiency, overtraining, context scaling, and inference efficiency retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 explains how sequence packing changes the data distribution across context lengths and removes the assertion that Transformers exhibit a larger performance drop across those contexts. Appendix E adds an interpretation of decreasing optimal token-to-parameter ratios through fitted exponents and learning-rate scheduling.

D1.justification: v2 specifies Grain first-fit packing and explicitly identifies chunk size L=64 and Fcausal=0.5 for FLOP accounting. Optimizer details repeated in Section 3.1 were already in Appendix A.1. The relocated reproducibility statement mentions experimental code and inference results upon acceptance, while the front-page code/data availability link remains.

R1.justification: Appendix E explicitly contrasts the decreasing optimal token-to-parameter ratio with Chinchilla's approximately constant ratio of 22 and connects the discrepancy to Porian et al. (2024). The cited-work set and main related-work discussion are retained; bibliography updates otherwise concern formatting and publication metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted prose edits expand explanations and clarify terminology. The reproducibility discussion moves from Appendix B into the main text, subsequent appendices are renumbered, and bibliographic formatting is standardized. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 23-25 and expands the captions of Figures 4-5. Existing plots and tables are retained with limited repositioning and text reflow, including Figure 12's vertical relocation, and conference headers are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit packing and FLOP-accounting details, clarifies the limits of cross-context loss comparisons, and makes existing scaling laws easier to apply through estimated configuration tables. These are useful but limited gains: the empirical validation remains unchanged, and the largest new estimates extrapolate beyond the trained model sizes.
